review_note: The official Governor press release identifies EO 01.01.2023.13 as the state-of-emergency declaration issued in preparation for Tropical Storm Ophelia.
Executive Order 01.01.2000.02 declares a storm emergency for a severe winter storm with blinding driving conditions and high winds; 01.01.2000.03 ends it on January 27, 2000.
Executive Order 01.01.2001.15 declares an emergency after tornadoes in Prince George's and Howard Counties.
Executive Order 01.01.2002.04 declares a drought emergency; later 2002 orders renew it.
Executive Order 01.01.2002.06 declares an emergency for the April 28, 2002 tornadoes (La Plata); 01.01.2002.07 adds Dorchester County the same day.
Executive Order 01.01.2004.51 declares a limited state of emergency in Cecil County for flooding from the remnants of Hurricane Ivan.
Executive Order 01.01.2008.11 declares a limited emergency for Tropical Storm Hanna; 01.01.2008.13 extends it statewide on September 5, 2008.
Executive Order 01.01.2009.16 declares an emergency for the effects of Tropical Storm Ida.
Executive Order 01.01.2009.21 declares an emergency in anticipation of severe winter weather; 01.01.2009.22 rescinds it on December 21, 2009.
Executive Order 01.01.2010.03 declares an emergency for severe winter weather; 01.01.2010.05 rescinds it on March 7, 2010.
Executive Order 01.01.2010.17 declares an emergency for Hurricane Earl.
Executive Order 01.01.2010.19 declares an emergency for the effects of Tropical Storm Nicole.
Executive Order 01.01.2010.24 declares an emergency for possible severe winter weather; 01.01.2010.25 rescinds it on December 28, 2010.
Executive Order 01.01.2011.02 declares an emergency due to flooding; 01.01.2011.03 rescinds it on March 14, 2011.
Executive Order 01.01.2011.17 continues the Irene emergency and declares one for flooding from Tropical Storm Lee.
Executive Order 01.01.2014.09 is headed June 13, 2014 (the compilation's list dates it April 1); 01.01.2014.10 rescinds it on June 20, 2014.
Executive Order 01.01.2018.01 declares a state of emergency for winter weather on the lower Eastern Shore; 01.01.2018.03 rescinds it on January 9, 2018.
